title: kit.canon-allow.v1
description: The reviewed allow-list of the canon scans (canon.allow.json): every entry names ONE instance (the file, the category, the literal exactly as reported and a piece of the line it sits on) with the reason a reviewer accepted it. There is no wildcard, no glob and no expiry: an entry that no longer matches anything is itself a problem (stale), so the list only shrinks.

file.description: Path relative to the repo root: one file, never a glob.

anyOf.description: A reviewed instance of a finding class (finding-classes.json) that its gate reports.

match.description: The literal exactly as the scan reports it. Never `*`: an allow entry is one instance.

context.description: A piece (4 or more characters) of the source line the literal sits on, so the entry names the instance and not every occurrence of the same literal in the file.

on.description: Category contrast only: the surface role the selector is used on. The theme gate then measures the selector on that surface instead of the page background, and it must read there.

in.description: Category contrast only: the container selector the selector is used in (its real ancestors, e.g. `.phone .phone__screen`). The theme gate builds the selector inside it and measures there.

reason.description: Why this instance is not hardcoding (a standard identifier, a published bin name, a protocol value, …). A follow-up that will remove it is not a reason: fix it instead.
